name: Pheromone cologne

lead: Pheromone colognes are fragrances or sprays marketed as containing human sex pheromones, with the promise of a more appealing presence and more attention from others. Buyers wear them as a scent-based add-on to grooming and presentation.

The idea draws on research into compounds such as androstenone and androstadienone, which come from sweat glands and are proposed to act through the vomeronasal organ or olfactory receptors. A widely cited encyclopedia summary says no pheromonal substance has been shown in a peer-reviewed study to directly influence human behavior, and the human vomeronasal organ is described as vestigial in adults.

paras: People wear them like any cologne or body spray, applied after showering and usually alongside regular grooming and a normal fragrance routine. Any effect users notice is typically judged by how others react in social settings.

Reported direct risks are those of any fragrance product, such as skin irritation or allergy in some users. Reviewers note that the attraction effect advertised by sellers is not demonstrated in peer-reviewed work.

forums.title: Does Your Sweat Turn Women On?

angle.text: Buyers wear these scents hoping the added pheromones make them more attractive and give them a more appealing presence, as a fragrance add-on to grooming. Reviewers report that no human pheromone has been shown to change behavior in a peer-reviewed study.

lead: Pheromone cologne is a perfume or body spray marketed with the claim that it contains human pheromones that make the wearer more sexually attractive. Wikipedia reports that such claims are unsupported by peer-reviewed evidence. [1]

The scientific literature on human pheromones centers on axillary steroids such as androstenol, androstenone and androstadienone, with some small studies reporting effects on mood or attention. Wikipedia notes the field has been criticized for small samples, publication bias and weak methods, and describes the role of human pheromones as speculative and controversial. [1]
In looksmaxxing circles, scent is sometimes discussed as one more component of appearance and presentation, and Wikipedia's article on looksmaxxing mentions offshoots such as smellmaxxing. [2]

paras: The word pheromone was coined in 1959. Wikipedia describes candidate human compounds, including androstenol, which a 1978 study associated with people rating photographed faces as warmer, and androstadienone, linked in some studies to mood and attention changes. [1] A 1971 report of menstrual synchrony was later questioned by reviewers. [1]

The article says the human vomeronasal organ appears atrophied or absent in adults and that its receptor genes are nonfunctional, while trace amine-associated receptors in the nose may detect certain volatile amines but their role in pheromone detection is not established. [1] Reviewers cited there, such as Hays (2003) and Bear and colleagues (2006), say there is no hard evidence that human pheromones alter sexual attraction. [1]
Some body-spray advertisers claim their products contain human sexual pheromones that act as aphrodisiacs; Wikipedia marks these claims as unsupported by peer-reviewed evidence. [1]

No studies found testing commercial pheromone colognes for attractiveness outcomes. Laboratory studies of individual compounds such as androstadienone have examined mood and attention in small groups, with variable results. [1]

timeline.event: Karlson and Luscher coin the term pheromone. [1]
